items.title: Section: Twenty Kinds of Mind, and the Sobering Speed With Which Freedom Collapses Back Into Craving

items.zh: 復次，當辯識身遍知。問：心清淨行苾芻，由幾種相遍知其心？答：若略說由三種相。一、雜染愛樂相，二、雜染過患相，三、雜染還滅方便善巧相。云何心清淨行苾芻，遍知自心雜染愛樂相？謂心清淨行苾芻作如是念：今我此心於諸雜染長夜愛樂。自知愛樂諸雜染已，便從有貪性出，於離貪性安止其心。爾時其心於離貪性不能安住，亦不愛樂，更無異緣，唯有速疾還來、趣入、流散、馳騁有貪性中。如從有貪性，如是從有瞋、有癡、下劣、掉舉、不寂靜、散亂性出，廣說乃至從放逸愛樂住性出，於常勤修習諸善法中安止其心。爾時其心於常勤修習諸善法中不能安住，亦不愛樂，更無異緣，唯有速疾還來、趣入、流散、馳騁乃至放逸愛樂性中。如是名為心清淨行苾芻，遍知自心雜染愛樂相。
items.en:
Second, distinguishing comprehensive knowledge; first, stating the topic. Furthermore, comprehensive knowledge of the forms of consciousness should be distinguished.
Second, explaining its characteristics; first, posing the question. Question: by how many characteristics does a monk practising for mental purity come to comprehensively know his own mind?
Second, answering; first, stating the list. Answer: in brief, through three characteristics: the characteristic of delighting in defilement, the characteristic of defilement's faults, and the characteristic of skilful means for defilement's cessation.
Second, explaining each in turn; first, the characteristic of delighting in defilement; first, posing the question. How does a monk practising for mental purity comprehensively know his own mind's characteristic of delighting in defilement?
Second, explaining; first, stating the reflection overall. Such a monk reflects thus: throughout the long night, this mind of mine has delighted in defilement.
Second, distinguishing each corresponding state; first, regarding a state of craving; first, withdrawing. Having recognised this delight in defilement, he withdraws from a state of craving and settles his mind in a state free of craving.
Second, returning. At that time, unable to remain settled in freedom from craving, taking no delight in it, his mind returns with a swiftness for which there is no analogy, rushes back, scatters, and races into the state of craving.
Second, regarding all the rest; first, withdrawing. As with a state of craving, so too withdrawing from hatred, delusion, a debased mind, agitation, unease, and scatteredness, extending through withdrawing from heedless delight, settling the mind in constant, diligent cultivation of wholesome dharmas.
Second, returning. At that time, unable to remain settled in constant, diligent cultivation of wholesome dharmas, taking no delight in it, his mind returns with a swiftness for which there is no analogy, rushes back, scatters, and races into heedless delight and the rest.
Third, concluding. This is called a monk practising for mental purity comprehensively knowing his own mind's characteristic of delighting in defilement.

items.title: Section: "If My Bowl Were Taken" — Recognising Defilement's Faults, and the Buddha's Own Question to a Meditating Monk

items.zh: 如是遍知自心雜染愛樂相已。此心清淨行苾芻，復能遍知自心雜染過患相。謂作是念：今我此有貪心，能為自害、能為他害、能為俱害，能生現法罪、能生後法罪、能生現法後法罪，又能為緣，生彼所生身心憂苦。如於有貪性，如是乃至於放逸愛樂性，當知亦爾。復作是念：此有貪心乃至放逸愛樂心，有過患故，有疫、有橫、有災、有惱。如是遍知自心雜染過患相已，復能遍知自心雜染還滅方便善巧相。謂我今不應隨自雜染，有諸過患、有疫、有橫、有災、有惱心自在轉，必令自心隨我勢力自在而轉。彼既如是了知，我今不應隨順自心而轉，當令自心隨我轉已，數數思擇，令有貪心捨有貪性，無貪性中安住愛樂，又復於彼見勝功德。如是乃至令捨放逸愛樂住性，乃至於常勤修習諸善法中安住愛樂，又復於彼見勝功德。
items.en:
Second, the characteristic of defilement's faults; first, stating. Having thus known his own mind's delight in defilement, this monk further comes to fully know his own mind's characteristic of defilement's faults.
Second, explaining; first, reflecting on the faults; first, presenting a craving mind. He reflects thus: this craving mind of mine can harm myself, can harm others, can harm both; can generate wrongdoing in this life, in future lives, or in both; and further serves as condition for the bodily and mental suffering thereby produced.
Second, extending to all the rest. As with a craving mind, so too through heedless delight, one should know the same.
Second, reflecting on equal-flow consequences. He further reflects thus: this craving mind, through heedless delight, having such faults, brings plague, hostility, calamity, and affliction.
Third, the characteristic of skilful means for cessation; first, stating overall. Having thus fully known his own mind's characteristic of defilement's faults, he further comes to fully know his own mind's characteristic of skilful means for defilement's cessation.
Second, explaining individually; first, presenting the means; first, through knowing. He reflects: I should not now follow my own defiled mind, with its faults, plague, hostility, calamity, and affliction, freely wherever it leads; I must instead cause my own mind to follow my own will freely.
Second, through careful investigation; first, regarding craving and freedom from craving. Having thus known that he should not follow his own mind but cause it to follow him, he repeatedly investigates, causing the craving mind to abandon craving and settle with delight in freedom from craving, recognising its superior qualities there.
Second, regarding every other state of mind. So too, extending through abandoning heedless delight and settling with delight in constant, diligent cultivation of wholesome dharmas, recognising its superior qualities there as well.

items.title: Section: When Virtue No Longer Needs Deliberation — And a Prisoner's Own Four Kinds of Chain

items.zh: 彼多安住如是行已，爾時其心不由思擇，於常懃修習諸善法中，自然安住愛樂；於前雜染愛樂性中，深生厭責。由此因緣，心清淨行苾芻，如實了知自心雜染愛樂速疾迴轉無譬喻性，又能善知如是雜染心有過患性，又能善知如是雜染心還滅方便。由如是故，心清淨行苾芻，速能證得無上心清淨性，所謂諸漏永盡。
items.en:
Third, through joy and aversion. Having dwelt extensively in this practice, his mind, without further deliberation, spontaneously settles with delight in constant, diligent cultivation of wholesome dharmas, feeling deep aversion and self-reproach towards his former delight in defilement.
Second, accomplishing skillfulness; first, clarifying thorough knowledge. Through this, a monk practising for mental purity truly knows his own mind's delight in defilement returning with incomparable speed, thoroughly knows this defiled mind's faults, and thoroughly knows the skilful means for its cessation.
Second, concluding the exhaustion of outflows. Through this, such a monk swiftly attains the very highest purity of mind, namely the permanent exhaustion of every outflow.

items.zh: 復次，當辯心善巧差別及心轉善巧差別。謂依遍計所執自性，當知心善巧差別；依依他起自性，當知心轉善巧差別。

items.title: Section: Two Benefits of Skilful Means, and Why the Four Foundations of Mindfulness Are Really About Observing a Single Mind

items.zh: 復次，若能善巧熏修心者，得二勝利。一、於果時觸證安樂，二、於因時自在而轉。復次，心混濁者有三過失。一、不如理作意過失，二、隨眠過失，三、起纏過失。問：如世尊言：唯當於心深善勇猛如理觀察。念住中說：要當於身住身循觀，乃至於法住法循觀。此何密意？答：為顯四念住唯觀察心故。謂觀心執受、觀心領納、觀心了別、觀心染淨。
items.en:
Second, revealing the benefit. Furthermore, whoever skilfully cultivates and habituates the mind attains two excellent benefits: first, personally verifying ease at the stage of fruition; second, turning freely at the stage of cause.
Third, clarifying its function; first, through observation; first, listing the faults. Furthermore, a turbid mind has three faults: the fault of improper attention, the fault of latent afflictive tendency, and the fault of actively arising affliction.
Second, clarifying the antidote; first, raising the scriptural question. Question: as the Blessed One said, one should observe the mind deeply, skilfully, and courageously according to reason; yet the foundations of mindfulness speak of dwelling in observation of the body, and so on through phenomena. What is the hidden intention here?
Second, explaining the answer; first, explaining the first statement. Answer: this is to reveal that the four foundations of mindfulness are solely about observing the mind — observing the mind that appropriates, the mind that receives, the mind that discerns, and the mind that gives rise to defilement and purity.

items.title: Section: "This Body Fundamentally Does Not Exist" — A Hell-Being's Own Liberating Words, and the Bodhisattva's Own Fourfold Mindfulness

items.zh: 唯為觀察心所執受、心所領納、心了別境、心染淨故，說四念住。
items.en: Second, explaining the second statement. The four foundations of mindfulness are taught solely to observe what the mind appropriates, what the mind receives, what the mind discerns as an object, and the mind's own defilement and purity.

blocks.text: A frank passage on how quickly a calm mind falls back into craving, and how virtue eventually becomes effortless.

Delight in defilement, its faults, and skilful means for its cessation. Master Cháng Bǎi: the return to defilement is so fast that nothing compares. For beginners, defilement flares easily and pure virtue is hard; beginningless habit is strong.
It harms self, others, both; generates wrongdoing; and brings suffering.
At last the mind "settles with delight" without deliberation. Master Cháng Bǎi: no more investigating; it dwells joyfully in purity.

Ease at the time of fruition and freedom at the time of cause. The bonds: improper attention, latent tendency, and arising affliction. (Untranslated, 0582c12: skill regarding the mind rests on the imagined nature; skill regarding its operation rests on the dependent nature.)
Master Cháng Bǎi: from four angles one observes the mind: as the body held, feeling received, mind discerning, and dharmas of defilement and purity.

Most practitioners know the experience: a calm sitting, and then one irritation and it is gone. The treatise names this honestly and does not treat it as failure. Virtue becomes effortless only with long habit.

quiz.q: By which three characteristics does such a monk know his mind?
options: delight in defilement, its faults, and skilful means for cessation
quiz.why: Delight in defilement, its faults, and skilful means for its cessation.

quiz.q: "With no other circumstance required." How does Master Cháng Bǎi take 更無異緣?
options: the speed of return to defilement is beyond any comparison
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: the return to defilement is so fast nothing compares, matching "incomparable speed" later. The English reads otherwise.

quiz.q: How does Master Cháng Bǎi describe the beginner's mind returning to craving?
options: defilement flares easily, pure virtue is hard; beginningless habit is strong
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: for beginners, defilement flares easily and pure virtue is hard; beginningless habit is strong.

quiz.q: How does the monk reflect on the faults of a craving mind?
options: it harms self, others, both, generating wrongdoing now and later, and suffering
quiz.why: It harms self, others, both, generates wrongdoing, and brings suffering.

quiz.q: What finally happens to the mind regarding wholesome dharmas?
options: without deliberation it settles with delight, feeling aversion towards former defilement
quiz.why: Without deliberation it settles with delight. Master Cháng Bǎi: no more investigating; it dwells joyfully in purity.

quiz.q: Which two benefits does one gain from habituating the mind?
options: ease at fruition, freedom at the causal stage
quiz.why: Ease at fruition and freedom at the causal stage.

quiz.q: What are the three faults of a turbid mind?
options: improper attention, latent tendency, arising affliction
quiz.why: Improper attention, latent tendency, and arising affliction.

quiz.q: Why are the foundations "solely about the mind," and how do they map?
options: the body the mind holds, feeling it receives, mind it discerns, and dharmas of defilement and purity it gives rise to
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: from four angles one observes mind: body held, feeling received, mind discerning, dharmas of defilement and purity.
